subject: Plot product term (ab) of bootstrapped mediation?

messages.author: 68ff531600bf84b8
messages.subject: Plot product term (ab) of bootstrapped mediation?
parts:
Hey all

I used bootstrapped CIs to test my indrect effects since the Sobel test requires the sampling distribution of the indirect effect to be normal... and we know, that this distribtuion tends to be asymmetric.

I wanted to extract all product terms from my bootstrapped.model.fit (5000 Iterations) in order to plot it... just to see if the 5000 product terms indeed are non normally distributed.
Anyhow, I have no idea how to extract the product terms... since I can't identify them with str(bootstrapped.model.fit) in the first place...

Can anyone show me how to access the bootstrapped prodcut terms?
something like: bootstrapped.model.fit@boot$coef -> but which are the prodcut terms?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Plot product term (ab) of bootstrapped mediation?
parts: and we know, that this distribtuion tends to be asymmetric.

In small samples, but is asymptotically normal.  Bootstrapping is often recommended to test indirect effects because it doesn't require this assumption, but bootstrapping is less efficient, at least because of Monte Carlo error.

Can anyone show me how to access the bootstrapped prodcut terms?
something like: bootstrapped.model.fit@boot$coef -> but which are the prodcut terms?

If "bootstrapped.model.fit" is the output of bootstrapLavaan(..., FUN = coef), then the column names are the estimated parameters.  You can create any user-defined parameters in the bootstrapLavaan() output by using the same definitions you used in the model syntax.  (It is probably easier if you save the bootstrapLavaan() output as a data.frame first, then add the user-defined parameters as new variables.)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: Plot product term (ab) of bootstrapped mediation?
parts:
Hi

There are a couple of recent articles addressing the use of bootstrap in assessing mediation:

Koopman, J., Howe, M., & Hollenbeck, J. R. (2014). Pulling the Sobel test up by its bootstraps. In C. E. Lance & R. J. Vandenberg (Eds.), More Statistical and Methodological Myths and Urban Legends (pp. 224–244). New York: Routledge.

Koopman, J., Howe, M., Hollenbeck, J. R., & Sin, H.-P. (2015). Small sample mediation testing: Misplaced confidence in bootstrapped confidence intervals. Journal of Applied Psychology, 100(1), 194–202.

The conclusion is basically that you should not trust bootstrap results too much unless you have a large sample. 

Mikko

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Plot product term (ab) of bootstrapped mediation?
parts: ...from your experience, what is todays "gold standard" of testing indirect effects?

I usually see citations for Kris Preacher and Andy Hayes supporting bootstrapping, but I have run small-scale simulations to demonstrate Monte Carlo techniques, and Sobel test seems to perform at least as well as bias-corrected bootstrap CIs even when N = 100 and using 3000 bootstraps.  So the articles Mikko posted definitely do not surprise me, and I think you could cite them to any reviewer who thinks bootstrapping is always preferable (assuming your data are reasonably similar to the conditions described by Koopman et al.).  But this question is better suited for SEMNET, where you might get a much larger and more diverse set of responses.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Plot product term (ab) of bootstrapped mediation?
parts: with FUN = coef, I can extract all parameters of interest (e.g. a1 & b1), but I won't get the parameterEstimates of my indriect effect (i.e., a1b1) as well as my total effect -> how can I extract coef and my bootstrapped CI of the indirect effect?

See my original response :-)  You can create any user-defined parameters in the bootstrapLavaan() output by using the same definitions you used in the model syntax.  (It is probably easier if you save the bootstrapLavaan() output as a data.frame first, then add the user-defined parameters as new variables.)

out <- as.data.frame(bootstrapLavaan(..., FUN = coef))
out$ab <- out$a * out*b
quantile(out$ab, probs = c(.025, .975))

Note that if you want a bias-corrected, accelerated CI, you can define a function that accepts your data frame and an arbitrary index variable to extract rows in a bootstrap sample, then fits the model and returns the coefficients, including (or only returning) the indirect effect.  Then you could use the boot() function directly (from the boot package), enabling you to extract the BCa CI using the boot.ci() function.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
